newsitem.title: UK: Willis Corroon profits rise 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Willis Corroon profits rise 17 pct.

text.p: Willis Corroon, the British-based international insurance broking group, on Wednesday reported a 17 percent rise in nine months pre-tax profits, and attributed the gains in part to the results of a recent internal review.

Pre-tax profits for the first nine months of the year climbed to 88.2 million pounds ($146 million) from 75.3 million and the group declared a fourth interim dividend of 1.65 pence per share -- unchanged from last year. ($1=.6050 Pound)

"The action the group has been taking to re-focus on its core businesses has achieved the objectives of improving profitability and strengthening the balance sheet, essential precursors to the next phase of the group's strategic development," executive chairman John Reeve said in a statement.
Willis at the half-year stage announced a number of measures to improve profitability. These included plans to develop a new organisational structure.
The group on Wednesday said it would make a charge of roughly eight million pounds against this year's profits in order to focus on short term initiatives designed to yield gains in 1997.

Willis said growth of brokerage and fees was two percent during the first nine months "in operating conditions which are recognised as being difficult for all insurance brokers". Cost controls helped improve operating margins.
